column3: Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “a mighty voice” and includes “every detestable beast.” “Lair” and “haunt” render κατοικητήριον (“dwelling”) and φυλακὴ (“prison”).
“Passion” renders θυμοῦ (“wrath”); “the extravagance of her luxury” renders “the power of her sensuality.”
“Contract” renders λάβητε (“receive”).
BSB follows the critical text with “piled up” (the Textus Receptus has “reached”).
“To others” is added; “pay her back double for what she has done” recasts “double to her the double according to her works.”
“The same measure of” renders τοσοῦτον (“so much”).
BSB has the present “judges,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the aorist κρίνας (“who has judged”).
“At the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her” renders “when they see the smoke of her burning.”
Close to the Greek.
“Will weep and mourn” renders the present “weep and mourn”; “there is no one left to buy” renders “no one buys any longer.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “spice” (amomum). “Olive oil” renders ἔλαιον.
BSB adds “And they will say”; “never to be seen again” recasts “they will certainly not find them any longer.”
“Sold these things” renders “of these things”; “grew their wealth” renders “were enriched.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “passenger” (“everyone who sails to a place”). “Will stand” renders the aorist “stood.”
BSB uses the future tense for the aorist and adds “they will exclaim”; “What city was ever like” renders “what [is] like.”
BSB uses the future tense for “they cast” and “were crying out.”
“Has pronounced for you His judgment against her” renders “has judged your judgment against her.”
“The size of” is added; “never to be seen again” renders “certainly not be found any longer.”
“Ring out” renders “be heard.”
BSB reverses “bridegroom and bride”; “call out” renders “be heard.”
Close to the Greek.
